lines:
Renders bounded, deterministic managed blocks from the canonical design model into a project's instruction files: the project root plus one block per folder containing bound files. Generation is opt-in per project and is driven by project open and settings changes. Blocks are wrapped in adashi markers, carry the design revision they were rendered from, and are overwritten on regeneration so external edits are transient.

Implemented Markdown extension (2026-09-25; SQLite and text backends): Extend the existing opt-in in-tree projection service to generate complete Markdown documents from a consistent canonical snapshot, default output directory docs/adashi with a configurable project-relative location. Preserve existing opt-in behavior and allow configuration through normal project settings. Use deterministic collision-safe paths derived from stable document identity so title edits do not break links. Every generated document starts with an agent note: Generated from Adashi; do not edit this file directly; Design ID and project identity; agents must retrieve the current document and readToken via Adashi MCP and save through adashi_design; direct edits are overwritten on regeneration. Include source content fingerprint/revision as freshness metadata without unrelated edit churn. Generated body preserves complete canonical Markdown without truncation or inserting the note into stored content. Existing root/folder shorts contain bounded titles/summaries and relative links to relevant documents; never inline entire bodies. Project docs are reachable from the root index; associations and direct bindings place links near relevant code. Track ownership locally; reject unsafe/out-of-checkout paths, symlink escapes, collisions and pre-existing unowned files. Atomic write-if-changed generation and owned-only cleanup handle delete, directory change and partial failure; preserve unrelated docs. External edits to owned generated files are detected/reported as drift and restored on regeneration, never imported. Refresh on canonical changes observed from MCP/desktop, project open and explicit regeneration/settings changes; unchanged canonical reads/projections do not dirty files. When projection fails, canonical data remains saved and a stale/missing/error status plus retry is visible. No bidirectional synchronization.

Verification (2026-09-25): Markdown tasks 25-36 implement this extension on the available SQLite and text adapters. Common contracts, actual stdio MCP, native Tauri/WebView2, conversion, independent Git clones and generated-file checks are recorded in task 36, QA jobs 6/7 and docs/markdown-validation.md. Generated files remain derived and agent authoring uses MCP. Server SQL implementation and validation remain pending in storage tasks 20-23.

Filename matching (2026-09-27): Resolve existing projection path components case-insensitively on every platform, preserve their on-disk spelling and reuse the existing file. Reject only genuinely ambiguous multiple matches, not a single differently capitalized name. Use the resolved paths for managed-block reads/writes, freshness checks, generated links and cleanup. Full-file ownership is case-insensitive so case-only settings changes and checkout renames retain ownership. Preserve handwritten text, reject unowned full-file outputs, and retain symlink/junction and project-boundary checks.
